title: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc in slight lead with more than 80% of votes counted
summary: While partial results show the pro-Netanyahu bloc ahead of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, the final tally could take days. Neither grouping is expected to win a majority, with tough coalition talks ahead.…
byline: Patrick Große, Mark Hallam, Felix Tamsut, Roshni Majumdar, Matt Ford

image.caption: Supporters of the main opposition party Yashar celebrate after exit polls suggested they were on course to win 21 seatsImage: Jack Guez/AFP

blocks.text: Situation barely moves as more than 80% of vote counted

Partial results published by the Central Elections Committee and reported by the Times of Israel newspaper showed the bloc led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on 54 seats, with 84.5% of votes counted.
The opposition bloc under Gadi Eisenkot of the centrist Yashar party was on 49 seats.
Neither bloc is set to received the 61 seats need for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, making some form of coalition likely.
The Arab-led parties — the Joint List and the United Arab List, commonly known under its Hebrew name of Ra’am — have dropped to 17 seats.
The numbers are still likely to change, particularly after a record number of absentee votes are counted.
The full tally of those will possibly not be confirmed until Friday, according to the newspaper.
